gaps.title: Prelude No. 4 in E minor, Op. 34 No. 4 (arr. Auerbach)
gaps.edition: Sikorski / Boosey & Hawkes: 'Five preludes arranged for violin and piano after op. 34' (Lera Auerbach, 2000), For Sale. Sikorski's 2004 '24 Präludien op. 34: Violine und Klavier' is probably the complete 24 (Tsyganov + Auerbach); not confirmed.
gaps.note: Completes the Tsyganov set. B&H/Sikorski sells 'Five preludes arranged for violin and piano after op. 34' (Lera Auerbach), and Wikipedia says Tsyganov transcribed 19 preludes for violin and piano in the 1930s and Auerbach arranged 'the remaining five' in 2000. The five numbers (4, 7, 9, 14, 23) are by elimination against the 19 existing Tsyganov entries; the publisher page does not list them. Set label kept identical to the Tsyganov entries so the 24 stay together (could be renamed '(arr. Tsyganov & Auerbach)' for all 24). Minutes approximate.

gaps.title: March (from Children's Notebook, Op. 69, arr. Fortunatov)
gaps.edition: Soviet edition arr. Konstantin Fortunatov (rights VAAP); listed in the Sikorski / Boosey & Hawkes catalogue as violin and piano
gaps.note: Same Fortunatov series as the Elegie already in the catalogue (id 1225; B&H lists it as 'The Human Comedy: Elegy') and probably the Gadfly Romance (id 1246). Only source is the B&H/Sikorski catalogue (item page gives publisher 'VAAP' and no edition number or year; some items show 'Information' only, i.e. not currently For Sale). Opus number from the Wikipedia list of compositions. Level and minutes are estimates. Borderline: a very easy children's piece, probably at or below ABRSM 3-4; drop if the catalogue judges it too easy. This item is For Sale at B&H.
